logline_en: An audio-first guessing game: everyday Korean sounds on a black screen with a countdown; the answer card appears only after the timer, inviting comments.

evidence.claim: Guide claims DM shares/saves/comments signal more than likes on Reels.
Short runtimes and replays reported as important.

hypotheses: H1: A participatory countdown increases comment rate relative to our account median.
H2: Culturally specific sounds increase sharing among Korean viewers more than among international viewers (compare KR vs non-KR share of views).
why_now: PROVISIONAL: no platform-measured candidates could be collected in this session (YouTube key missing, Instagram/Apify hosts blocked); evidence below is secondary and unverified. Re-rank against measured clusters before production spend. Tests a participation mechanic that does not depend on any trending audio.
creative_principle: Withhold the visual answer behind a short timer so the viewer commits to a guess, then reward them; the comment section becomes the scoreboard.
originality_notes: All sounds are recorded by us from objects we own or public places where recording is permitted; no platform sounds, jingles or branded voice prompts are used.
format: audio quiz, black screen + waveform + countdown, answer reveal cards
hooks_ko: 이 소리 3초 안에 맞히면 한국 사람
edit_plan: Fixed 4.8 s rhythm per question so the pattern is learned by question 2; last question breaks the rhythm.
audio_plan: Clean field recordings (phone + windscreen), each normalised to -16 LUFS; countdown ticks synthesized; master -14 LUFS.
success_metric: Comment rate ≥ 2× account median; ≥ 30% of comments state a score.
risks: Recording in shops or transit may need permission
Sounds may be too ambiguous without testing on 3–5 people first
